scope: Explicit collaborating LLM agents; DB conferences, 2024–2026 publication years; identified mechanisms only; one primary layer.

entries.mechanism: Identify redundant exploration and share compatible work across agents.
entries.mas_evidence: Supervisor and field agents; the proposal explicitly considers sharing across agents and turns.
entries.limitation: A research vision with motivating cases; no completed general MAS planner is established.

entries.mechanism: Prepare subtask requirements, prerequisite queries and constraints before handing work to execution agents.
entries.mas_evidence: A Task Interpreter Agent prepares work for an Analysis Executor Agent; a Process Supervisor Agent checks the process and returns errors.
entries.limitation: Retain only the task/prerequisite preparation mechanism. Its cost-based optimization of data operators is not evidence of optimizing agent topology. The demo does not independently evaluate a general dependency extractor.

entries.mechanism: Rewrite agent workflow graphs and schedule execution to reuse shared computation.
entries.mas_evidence: Evaluates multi-agent debate, expert/critic reflection and expert/summarizer collaboration.
entries.limitation: Starts from a supplied DAG, with one base model and local operations; deterministic caching rules do not establish arbitrary semantic equivalence.

entries.mechanism: Jointly choose agent topology, models and execution engines under cost, latency and quality objectives.
entries.mas_evidence: Uses a real 10-agent pipeline and discusses dependencies between collaborating agents.
entries.limitation: The integrated optimization loop is a research agenda, not a completed and comprehensively evaluated optimizer.

entries.mechanism: Use workflow state to choose the next agent and control retries and termination.
entries.mas_evidence: User, Planner, Engineer, Executor and Critic exchange outputs and feedback under a common scheduler.
entries.limitation: Only its scheduling mechanism is retained. Its tabular-QA accuracy is application-specific; it is not a general resource scheduler.

entries.mechanism: Represent and orchestrate multi-agent execution using a declarative workflow DAG.
entries.mas_evidence: The demonstration has a planner, three analysis agents and an aggregation agent; AWEL explicitly expresses multi-agent execution plans.
entries.limitation: Retain the AWEL and multi-agent orchestration design. The demo does not establish a cost-based MAS optimizer or performance guarantees.

entries.mechanism: Compile agent workflows, check dependencies and schemas, and run independent branches in parallel.
entries.mas_evidence: Autonomous AgentNodes have private contexts and standardized input/output ports; a global planner and workflow engine coordinate them with ToolNodes.
entries.limitation: Retain the DBMS-inspired workflow engine, not the analytics application. The demo describes the design without a standalone scheduler benchmark.

entries.mechanism: Exchange structured information through a shared buffer and route it to the relevant agents.
entries.mas_evidence: A proxy and specialized agents communicate while completing a common BI task.
entries.limitation: Only the evaluated communication component is retained. Its notebook-cell DAG retrieves context rather than extracting a future collaboration plan.

entries.mechanism: Summarize agents' execution records and exchange concise evidence for cross-review.
entries.mas_evidence: Several selected LLM experts analyze the same anomaly, exchange summarized procedures/results and revise their findings through cross-review.
entries.limitation: Retain the coordination and message-preparation mechanism. Database diagnosis itself is MAS for DB, and generic MAS-wide gains are not established.

entries.mechanism: Use a shared result pool and quality statistics to choose which agent team runs next.
entries.mas_evidence: Generation, Expansion and Management teams coordinate; a Management Agent consumes a Critical Agent's evaluation and changes the active team.
entries.limitation: Retain its data-driven team scheduling and shared result-pool mechanism. SQL diversity, executability and coverage remain application-specific criteria.

entries.mechanism: Check prerequisites and execution constraints, control recovery, and bound agent interaction loops.
entries.mas_evidence: A Coordinator Agent orchestrates Database/Query, Visualization Implementation and Validation/Evaluation agents through feedback.
entries.limitation: Retain the rule-governed collaboration mechanism and its ablation. Visualization is the application, not a fourth survey dimension. Bounded termination is not a guarantee that every generated answer is correct.

entries.mechanism: Validate each agent output against its input and upstream results before passing it to downstream agents.
entries.mas_evidence: Extraction, Generation, Refinement and Alignment agents exchange intermediate results; §3.1 explicitly addresses error accumulation across collaborating agents.
entries.limitation: Retain only inter-agent consistency checking and correction. The rules and evaluation are Text-to-SQL-specific; this is not a general MAS correctness guarantee. Section references use the author preprint, whose layout differs from the published article.

entries.mechanism: Record linked interaction and execution traces for monitoring, replay and failure inspection.
entries.mas_evidence: Planner, Context Retrieval, Knowledge Retrieval, SQL Generator and SQL Validator exchange context, drafts and feedback.
entries.limitation: Retain structured trace collection and inspection. The demo does not prove general causal error attribution or an evaluated automatic root-cause algorithm.

related_publications.note: UNITQA is related to AutoTQA and describes five agents with FSM scheduling. Official demo-list metadata and the existing indexed abstract were checked; its full paper was unavailable in this pass. Keep as a related publication, not another independently verified scheduler.

Demo of MultiVis-Agent. The author institution confirms the central coordinator and logic-rule design. The research paper supplies the detailed mechanism and ablation evidence; do not count the demo as another method.

boundary_cases.reason: Official ICDE 2026 DEFT publication metadata is verified. Publisher access did not expose the paper; secondary summaries do not justify a confirmed mechanism or layer.
AdaCoAgentEA's author repository confirms collaborating agents and communication protocols, but detailed primary-paper evidence on what the protocol manages and how it is evaluated is still missing.

boundary_cases.status: Planning-related boundary · not admitted as MAS optimization
boundary_cases.reason: Carnot §2.3 confirms a QueryPlanner, a data-discovery subagent and an LLM-assisted optimizer. Its inspected optimization/revision machinery targets semantic query operators; a separate collaboration-support mechanism is not sufficiently established.

boundary_cases.status: Planning-related application · outside the main list
boundary_cases.reason: AutoPrep has cooperating Planner and Programmer agents, but its logical plan describes data-preparation operations. Those plans are not automatically MAS collaboration plans.

boundary_cases.status: Planning-related application · outside the main list
boundary_cases.reason: DocETL uses generation and validation agents to optimize document-processing plans. Using a MAS as the optimizer does not establish optimizing the MAS itself.

boundary_cases.status: Planning-related optimizer · outside the main list
boundary_cases.reason: MOAR searches semantic-operator rewrites. Its plan cost/quality objectives alone do not establish a collaborating MAS as the optimized object.
Credo manages beliefs, policies and LLM pipeline operators. Mentioning AutoGen in related work does not establish a collaborating MAS in the demonstrated system.
AgenticScholar has a hybrid planner and composable operators. The inspected primary text does not establish multiple collaborating autonomous agents.
Mil schedules multiple-model applications; ensembling, routing and chained summarization do not by themselves establish a cooperating LLM MAS.

boundary_cases.status: Confirmed MAS workload support · primary layer: Inference Infrastructure
boundary_cases.reason: HEXGEN-FLOW v3 evaluates CHESS-style workflows and MAC-SQL. MAC-SQL explicitly has collaborating agents. Restore MAS-support evidence, but its optimized object is inference-request serving, so do not force it into Planning or Execution.

boundary_cases.status: Supporting Planning algorithm · primary layer remains Action
boundary_cases.reason: SagaLLM Algorithm 1 constructs roles and dependencies; keep this as a chapter reference. Its principal contribution remains transactional compensation/recovery; no duplicate primary entry is added.

boundary_cases.status: Execution-related application · outside the main list
boundary_cases.reason: SAGA partitions generation tasks into time blocks; its replay engine labels anomalies in generated graph data. This is not evidence of recovering erroneous MAS executions or synchronizing arbitrary agent state.

The abstract and introduction establish modular benchmarking of NL2SQL algorithms, including cost and latency. They do not establish a MAS-specific collaboration-analysis mechanism; a multi-agent benchmarking implementation alone is insufficient.

limitations: The list is bounded by inspected sources, not exhaustive.
Application components are not claims that the whole application is DB for MAS.
Demo descriptions and visions do not establish general experimental performance.
Original abstracts remain in the existing library; absent originals are not fabricated.
